name: Diablo
strap: Enter Sanctuary. Leave the checklist behind.
description: Where to start Diablo, why each entry point works, what to skip, and the lore and characters worth knowing.
intro: Choose a campaign and a class that appeal to you. Sanctuary’s history adds flavour, but it does not require decades of loot hunting before your first adventure.
recommendation: Begin with Diablo IV’s base campaign for the modern story, then its expansions in order. Choose Diablo II: Resurrected for the classic atmosphere and build-focused game.
basics: The human world lies between the ambitions of Heaven and Hell. Neither side’s claim to righteousness guarantees humanity’s safety.
Diablo, Mephisto, and Baal are distinct demons associated with terror, hatred, and destruction.
A campaign teaches the world and your class. Seasonal progression, higher difficulties, and perfect equipment are separate commitments.

entries.title: Diablo IV base campaign
entries.why: A new wanderer and a clear conflict introduce Sanctuary through people living in it. The campaign supplies the relationships its expansions need.
entries.need: Lilith has returned; humanity is caught between powerful beings with competing plans.
entries.skip: Diablo I–III, their difficulty ladders, and seasonal completion.
entries.tradeoff: Start with the base campaign if you care about the story rather than using campaign-skip options.
entries.next: Play Vessel of Hatred, then Lord of Hatred. Explore endgame activities when you want more.

entries.title: Diablo II: Resurrected
entries.audience: I want the classic dark adventure
entries.why: Its journey across several regions gives a clear objective and a strong sense of a world under siege. The remaster retells Diablo II and Lord of Destruction.
entries.need: A mysterious wanderer is carrying danger east from Tristram.
entries.skip: The original Diablo, unless its small-town horror appeals to you. A recap is sufficient.
entries.tradeoff: Older combat, resource management, and skill decisions demand more patience than Diablo IV.
entries.next: Finish the main campaign, then Lord of Destruction. Choose further difficulty runs for the gameplay, not new required story.

entries.title: Diablo III and Reaper of Souls
entries.audience: I want brisk action and an approachable campaign
entries.why: Readable objectives and spectacular combat make this a straightforward introduction to the conflict.
entries.need: Demons threaten Sanctuary, and a fallen star draws adventurers to Tristram.
entries.skip: Diablo I–II, challenge ladders, and seasonal optimisation.
entries.tradeoff: Its brighter presentation differs from Diablo I and IV. Reaper of Souls is the next story chapter.
entries.next: Play the five-act story across the base game and expansion, then stop or enter Adventure Mode.

events.title: Diablo
events.premise: A traveller descends beneath a town whose cathedral conceals a growing horror.
events.recap: The hero defeats Diablo but attempts to contain him by taking the soulstone into himself. The apparent victory creates the danger pursued in Diablo II.
events.why: Optional origin story; a short recap supplies the bridge.

events.title: Diablo II
events.premise: A new hero follows corruption spreading across Sanctuary.
events.recap: The chase leads to the Prime Evils: Mephisto and Diablo are defeated, while Baal’s campaign threatens the Worldstone.
events.why: Start here for the classic journey, then continue into its expansion.

events.title: Lord of Destruction
events.premise: Baal’s forces advance on the Worldstone.
events.recap: Baal is defeated, but the Worldstone has been corrupted. Tyrael destroys it to prevent that corruption consuming Sanctuary.
events.why: The conclusion to Diablo II’s campaign.

events.title: Diablo III
events.premise: A fallen star and renewed demonic activity draw heroes to New Tristram.
events.recap: Diablo uses Leah as his vessel and attacks Heaven. The hero defeats him, while the Black Soulstone remains dangerous.

events.title: Reaper of Souls
events.premise: Malthael turns the Black Soulstone against humanity.
events.recap: The hero defeats Malthael. The struggle exposes how an angel’s solution can threaten Sanctuary as severely as a demon’s.
events.why: Finish after Diablo III; it adds the fifth act.

events.title: Diablo Immortal
events.premise: Adventurers pursue fragments of the shattered Worldstone.
events.recap: The launch campaign turns the Worldstone’s destruction into a continuing struggle over its fragments. Its live-service stories extend beyond this orientation.
events.why: Optional mobile/MMO-style branch, not a prerequisite for the numbered games.

events.title: Diablo IV
events.premise: A wanderer enters the conflict between Lilith, Inarius, and the people following them.
events.recap: Lilith is defeated, but Neyrelle leaves with Mephisto’s soulstone. Ending one immediate threat carries another into the expansion story.

events.title: Vessel of Hatred
events.premise: The search for Neyrelle continues into a region marked by Mephisto’s influence.
events.recap: Neyrelle’s struggle with the soulstone makes Mephisto the centre of the continuing arc. This summary introduces the bridge without retelling every expansion reveal.
events.why: Play after Diablo IV’s base campaign.

events.title: Lord of Hatred
events.premise: The continuing confrontation with Mephisto reaches the islands of Skovos.
events.why: Follow Vessel of Hatred; this guide covers the released expansion’s setup rather than inventing its ending.

characters.name: Diablo
characters.motivation: Fear is both his weapon and the shape of his influence.
characters.relationships: Mephisto and Baal are the other Prime Evils.

updates.text: The soulstone victory becomes the Dark Wanderer’s tragedy.

characters.name: Mephisto
characters.motivation: He benefits when mistrust turns communities against themselves.
characters.relationships: His ties to Lilith and Neyrelle matter increasingly in Diablo IV.

updates.text: His soulstone becomes Neyrelle’s burden after Lilith’s defeat.

characters.name: Baal
characters.motivation: His campaign attacks Sanctuary’s foundations rather than merely its inhabitants.
characters.relationships: His story intersects with Tyrael and the Worldstone.

updates.text: Corruption of the Worldstone survives his defeat.

characters.name: Deckard Cain
characters.motivation: He uses inherited knowledge to help ordinary heroes confront ancient threats.
characters.relationships: Leah and Tyrael connect his scholarship to later events.

characters.name: Tyrael
characters.motivation: He repeatedly questions whether cosmic duty serves the people at risk.
characters.relationships: The Horadrim carry much of his work into Sanctuary.

characters.name: Lilith
characters.role: A figure tied to Sanctuary’s origins
characters.motivation: Her claim to protect humanity comes with coercion and ruthless demands.
characters.relationships: Inarius and Mephisto define competing parts of her history.

updates.text: The wanderer rejects her proposed future for Sanctuary.

characters.name: Inarius
characters.role: An angel revered by the Cathedral of Light
characters.motivation: His desire to return to Heaven shapes what he asks of his followers.
characters.relationships: Lilith and the Cathedral’s believers are central to his story.

characters.name: Leah
characters.motivation: She wants to understand the dangers surrounding Tristram while keeping a future beyond them.
characters.relationships: Cain’s research and her family history place her inside the third game’s conflict.

updates.text: Diablo’s plan uses her as a vessel, turning her personal history into the campaign’s tragedy.

characters.name: Neyrelle
characters.motivation: She wants the knowledge to make choices larger powers would reserve for themselves.
characters.relationships: The wanderer supports her; Mephisto tests the cost of that independence.

updates.text: She takes responsibility for Mephisto’s soulstone.

factions: A scholarly order associated with containing demonic threats. Their history explains the soulstones without making the novels compulsory.
Their struggle predates the games. Sanctuary’s people have interests that do not neatly match either side.
A faith centred on Inarius. Its promises should be understood through the people who follow it.
timeline_help: Release order and story order differ for Immortal, which sits between Diablo II and III. The starting-route filter highlights the numbered campaigns and their story expansions; it is not a demand to finish them all. Individual completion settings reveal only that entry.
scope: Covers the numbered games, Lord of Destruction, Reaper of Souls, Vessel of Hatred, Lord of Hatred, and Immortal’s launch premise. Lord of Hatred coverage is introductory, not a full ending recap. Resurrected is a retelling; Reign of the Warlock adds gameplay and a class rather than a new numbered campaign here. Hellfire, Immortal updates, and seasonal stories are outside this route.
